title: Exactness closure of globally constructible pro-etale module sheaves
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Work in the abelian category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_Y$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Use precisely the global finite-stratification constructibility predicate [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], including a positive number of strata. If $f:F\to G$ is a morphism between constructible module sheaves, then $\ker f$ and $\operatorname{coker}f$ are constructible. If $S$ is a short exact sequence $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$ of module sheaves and $F,G$ are constructible, then $E$ is constructible. The scheme and the coefficient ring may be empty and zero, respectively.

proof.text: Apply proEtaleModuleRestriction_constructible_iff from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-module-constructibility] to identify intrinsic constructibility with fixed-module constructibility over ULift A. The proved coefficient_constructible_iff helper of [lem-weil-constructible-coefficient-serre] identifies coefficient-universe intrinsic constructibility over the same ring with precisely that fixed-module predicate. Its restriction functor at ULift A is definitionally the small-coefficient restriction functor. Compose these two equivalences of propositions. The constant ring sheaves and module categories are definitionally identical, so no sheaf or morphism is transported. Both comparison lemmas preserve the global finite-partition convention, including the empty scheme and positive stratum count.

Specialize constructibleCoefficient_exactClosure of [lem-weil-constructible-coefficient-serre] to the finite commutative ring ULift A. For a map between intrinsic constructible sheaves, translate both hypotheses using step 1, apply the kernel/cokernel clause, and translate the two conclusions back. For a short exact complex, translate its outside terms, apply the extension clause, and translate its middle term back. The short complex, its maps, its kernel and cokernel are unchanged because the two module categories are definitionally equal. This proves both required clauses without any new lemma or additional finiteness, nonemptiness or nonzero-ring hypothesis.

lean.statement:
theorem constructibleProEtale_exactClosure
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] :
    (∀ (F G : proEtaleRingModules Y (proEtaleConstantRing Y A)) (f : F ⟶ G),
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A F →
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A G →
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A (kernel f) ∧
        IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A (cokernel f)) ∧
    (∀ S : ShortComplex (proEtaleRingModules Y (proEtaleConstantRing Y A)),
      S.ShortExact → IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A S.X₁ →
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A S.X₃ →
      IsConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf Y A S.X₂)
